newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - DLJ cuts CSX estimates.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - DLJ cuts CSX estimates.

text.p: -- Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette analyst James Higgins cut his earnings estimates for CSX Corp to $3.90 a share from $4 for 1996, and to $4 from $4.45 for 1997, citing earnings dilution from CSX's proposed merger with Conrail Inc.
-- "We think the valuation on Conrail is quite rich," Higgins said in a report.
-- Longer-term prospects are "potentially quite favorable," but there are "significant risks whose expected value we cannot quantify at this time," he said.
-- The companies' projections for gains on incremental revenues are based on "quite an aggressive increase" of 80 percent from Conrail's intermodal revenues over a four-year period, Higgins said.

-- The greatest risk is the level of competitive concessions the two railroads will be required to grant to obtain federal approval. Norfolk Southern Corp is the potential beneficiary of any moves to increase competition in the northeastern United States, and a strong Norfolk Southern presence could compromise Conrail's value, he said.

-- "We agreed with CSX officials who stated on October 2 that additional rail mergers would be ill advised given the rise in shipper calls for open access to railroad networks where there is no competition. We still agree with that warning," he said.
-- A proforma earnings projection by DLJ forecast earnings per share for the combined firm of $4.65 in 1998, $5.59 in 1999, $6.48 in 2000 and $7.01 in 2001.
